title: In the reprobate even the least sins will be punished eternally
source_text: II. Imo docent in reprobis & impoenitentibus, peccata quaelibet, etiam minima, quale est verbum otiosum, poena aeterna actu & reipsa aliquando punienda esse. Juxta illud Christi in Evangelio, Dico autem vobis, quoniam omne verbum otiosum, quod locuti fuerint homines, reddent rationem de eo in die judicii. Nec enim, ex communi Christianarum Scholarum doctrina, post diem judicii, ulli alii poenae quam aeternae locus erit.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover they teach that in the reprobate and impenitent any sins whatever, even the least, such as an idle word, are sometime to be punished with eternal penalty in act and in very deed. According to that of Christ in the Gospel, But I say to you that every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account of it in the day of judgment. For neither, by the common doctrine of Christian schools, after the day of judgment will there be place for any other penalty than the eternal.
pass_b_english: For the impenitent, even idle words meet everlasting punishment in fact after judgment.
Christian schools agree: past that day only eternal penalty remains.

lemmas.gloss: in act and in very deed

choices.why: Technical Reformed term for those left under wrath.
